shortDescription: Nordic forward prices fell on Tuesday, retreating from multi-year highs as lower European gas prices and forecasts for wetter weather across Scandinavia weighed on the market.

children: Nordic forward prices fell on Tuesday, retreating from multi-year highs as lower European gas prices and forecasts for wetter weather across Scandinavia weighed on the market.
The Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) was down €2.68, or 2.28%, at €114.75 per megawatt hour (MWh)at 09:22 GMT, after hitting its highest level since December 2022 on Monday.
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) lost €0.58, or 0.83%, to €69.1 MWh.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices eased from near four-year highs but remain supported by ongoing disruptions to liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply from the Middle East and Europe's efforts to replenish gas storage.

On the weather front, "The rest of this week will be under ongoing low-pressure influence with unsettled, wet, and windy weather in the entire Scandinavia. Temperatures will be near normal, accompanied by largely above-normal rain amounts," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 12.27 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, compared with 11.46 TWh below normal on Monday.
Germany's year-ahead power (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark contract, fell €4.03, or 2.95%, to €132.5 per MWh.
